tickets.title: Catalogue loads whose storage calls are bounded by the shards they touch, sent in parallel and published once (**amendment 13, E25, 2026-10-28; design R-P549**)

authority.locator: E25 · section 2 of amendment 13, "Done when" (lane L20's finding, R-P540; the diagnosis S42/analyst-503, R-P543; in force by section 3 row 1, R-P544); the owner's direction of 28 October (R-P545 (2): the retry-and-pool design withdrawn, the load redesigned around its root cause) and the design adopted from the root-cause analysis (R-P549: design C, one pack per load, and design C2, staged files published once)
authority.requirement: a failed storage call on the load's path is retried once inside the request (bounded, idempotent: exact-creates and reads only); the load's calls run in a bounded pool without batch barriers; the 503 names the operation, the object kind and the storage error's number (never a key or a body) and a `state` — `nothing_written`, `pending` (recover) or `committed`; the `changed` count compares records independent of field order; the purge collects the objects a refused load left once they are older than the grace; kit 02 and kit 03 state the load protocol (file size, client timeout, read the status then recover or re-send); the live walk measures the refusal rate and the time per 5,000 products on both pair hosts, one host at a time.

tickets.outcome: A catalogue load writes one pack instead of one object per product, so its storage calls are bounded by the shards it touches and not by its product count; 40,000 products land as staged files sent in parallel and published once in about half a minute, never refused for one transient storage failure, with an exact changed count, a 503 that names its cause and state, nothing left behind that the purge does not collect, a product page as cheap as today, and no operator step for the catalogues stored today.

criteria.observable: On both hosts in the harness, over a catalogue stored in packs, a load of a 5,000-product file makes at most 40 storage calls whatever the catalogue's size (at N = 5,000 and at N = 40,000 its calls differ by at most 10), and so does a load of 100 or 1,000 new products and one of 5,000 changed products; a re-send of an unchanged 5,000-product file (the skip) makes at most 15. A load writes one pack, the one content-addressed object holding every part whose digest moved and every product shard and id shard it rebuilt, each object inside it addressed by its pack and byte range and checked by its own digest, beside the publication's own writes (the head reservation, the revision, the set and the head commit); a pack is at most 64 MiB (a load past it refused 413 load_too_large, nothing written) and the four 2 MiB refusals (part_too_large, index_shard_too_large, id_index_too_large, manifest_too_large) answer as today. Every catalogue behaviour answers as today (status, code, changed, the skip, the dry run and the revision: the refusals of an id in two places, the per-product modes, ?product=, ?shard=, the PUT round trip, removeProducts; the 26 steps of the design's behaviour probe, LOCK), and the bounded rollback counts packs: undoing a 5,000-product reload at 40,000 products answers 200 within 40 calls. Measured on the prototype: 23–32 calls for 5,000 new products, 23–24 for 5,000 changed, 13 for the skip, 24 for 100, 25 for 1,000, the rollback 200 in 25 (_evidence/parity-step3/S44/analyst-load/logs/summary.txt:56–61, :70–71, :116). Today a load makes one exact-create per changed product's part (src/routes/content.ts:263–266; src/config/publication.ts:658–668, :611–614), one read per touched shard and id shard, one product and one id at a time (content.ts:303–320, :1468–1471, :1478–1486), and one exact-create per moved shard (content.ts:376–379; publication.ts:832–844): 6,044 calls for 5,000 new products, 10,532 for 5,000 changed, 5,267 for the skip, 448 for 100, 2,020 for 1,000 (_evidence/parity-step3/S44/analyst-load/logs/summary.txt:11–15), and the rollback is refused 413 rollback_too_large after 774 calls (content.ts:543–597; _evidence/parity-step3/S44/analyst-load/logs/summary.txt:108).
criteria.proof: The P98 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P98.LD1 in src/units/P98/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: On both hosts in the harness, 40,000 products sent as staged files of up to 5,000 products each (within today's input caps of 2 MiB and 10,000 records a request, src/config/input.ts:2–3, unchanged), sent in parallel, and then published once, make at most 250 storage calls in all and one publication (one head reservation and one commit); a stage writes its pack and publishes nothing, the publish merges the stages, runs the refusals of an id in two places across them (record_moved, id_in_part, id_shared, as today across one file) and commits them in one compare-and-set; the stage and publish doors admit the catalogue-import credential as the import does (content.ts:77–85). No load, stage or publish is refused for one transient failure of a safe-to-repeat call: every GET and HEAD, the pack's exact-create (an existing pack adopted when its size and digest match) and the revision and set exact-creates (publication.ts:611–614, :899–903) are retried once inside the request; the head's compare-and-set is never re-sent blindly (on a throw the head is re-read and a request whose pending set it holds is finished, publication.ts:987–988, :1066–1077; a lost race answers 409 as today); two consecutive failures of one call answer LD4's 503. Today nothing is retried (grep -n -i "retry\|setTimeout\|timeout" src/config/publication.ts: comment lines only, :625, :656, :721, :831, :1014), one failed call refuses the load (lane L20: 29 of 193 fill loads refused, about 1 call in 8,000; R-P540, R-P543), 40,000 products in eight files make 47,843 calls (_evidence/parity-step3/S44/analyst-load/logs/summary.txt:9) and took about 27 minutes live with re-sends; under design C the eight files published one by one make 182 calls (_evidence/parity-step3/S44/analyst-load/logs/summary.txt:55); C2 is not prototyped, and its live time (about 10–15 s, a HYPOTHESIS from S42's fitted latencies, _evidence/parity-step3/S44/analyst-load/DESIGN.md §9) is measured in LV1 against 30 s.
criteria.proof: The P98 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P98.LD2 in src/units/P98/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: The 503 a storage failure on the load's path answers (a load, a stage or the publish) names its cause and the state it left: the operation, the object's kind, the storage error's status where known, and state, one of nothing_written, pending (recover with POST /content/catalog/publication/recover) and committed, matching the store in each scenario (_evidence/parity-step3/S44/analyst-load/DESIGN.md §6: before the pack PUT nothing; the PUT landed then threw, one unnamed pack; after the reservation, a pending head finished in the same request), and never an object key, a body or a token. criteria.observable: The changed count is exact: on both hosts a one-product retitle answers changed equal to the records it changed, on a fresh isolate and on a warm one, in the committed answer and in the dry run, whether the product's part is in a pack or still a part of its own. Today changedPieces compares JSON.stringify strings (src/routes/content.ts:1013–1018) of the stored part, read back in canonical key order (src/config/publication.ts:88–93, :674–684) or held in the validator's order by the isolate that wrote it (:665), against the validator's output (content.ts:1522–1551), so a cold isolate counts every record of the product (live: changed 1199 for one retitle, R-P540; harness: 5 of 5 cold, 1 warm, _evidence/parity-step3/S42/analyst-503/DIAGNOSIS.md §4); the answers at content.ts:1663 and :1676 carry it.

criteria.observable: A refused load or stage, and a stage never published, leaves nothing the pack-aware purge does not collect: its pack, the only object it writes before the head is reserved, is deleted once no stored revision's pack table names it and it was uploaded 15 minutes ago or more (the grace, ATTACHMENT_GRACE_MS, src/config/publication.ts:1439); the manifest's pack table names every pack the revision reaches with its live objects and bytes, so the purge deletes packs by the tables of the stored revisions and a listing, reading no shard; a pack under a quarter live, or past 64 packs in the table, is re-homed by a later load. A pack named by any stored revision, or by the pending set the head holds, is never deleted, and a pack that a load or stage in flight reuses is never collected (the reusing request heads it again after reserving the head and writes it again if it is gone; the purge stops before a deletion while the head holds a pending set). The objects stored before packs (l3's leftovers included) are collected once no stored revision names an object without a range: one full reload repacks the rest (R-P549; amendment 13 section 3 row 3). Today the purge reaches only the objects a purged revision named (orphansOf, publication.ts:1376–1411) and lists only their directories (sweep, :1420–1437), so an object no revision ever named is never collected (187 objects survived 12 publications, _evidence/parity-step3/S42/analyst-503/DIAGNOSIS.md §4), and an exact-create that adopts an existing object keeps its old upload time (publication.ts:611–614, :1441–1447).
criteria.proof: The P98 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P98.LD6 in src/units/P98/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

tickets.title: The purge at scale (**amendment 13, E23, 2026-10-28**)

authority.locator: E23 · section 2 of amendment 13, "Done when" (P93's delivery review, R-P506; P95's delivery review, R-P531; in force by section 3 row 1, R-P544)
authority.requirement: the purge keeps its progress across passes so a large revision is removed over several publications; the latent delete order (shard keys queued before the parts behind them) cannot strand a part; a tenant whose salt count can never be established is told (an advisory on the operator's reads) and its learn revisions purged past a stated bound once the count is null for good, or the owner's alternative.

tickets.outcome: The purge removes every revision past the tenant's setting however large its load was, without stranding a part, and a tenant whose salt count can never be established is told so and does not keep every learn revision for good.

criteria.observable: On both hosts, a tenant under the configuration-revision setting whose catalogue holds 40,000 products and whose stored revisions include loads that each touched all 256 product shards and 256 id shards (eight 5,000-product loads, as P93's delivery review loaded them): once those revisions are past the setting, each is removed, its body and the shards and parts only it names, over a bounded number of later publications, each publication's purge within its own budget (PURGE_OPERATIONS 256 and PURGE_BYTES, src/config/publication.ts:1273–1274, :1281) and its progress kept from one publication to the next; nothing another stored revision names is removed and nothing is left that no stored revision names. Today each publication's purge starts afresh: orphansOf reads every shard a revision names, one budget call each (publication.ts:1376–1386), before sweep lists or deletes anything (:1420–1437), so a revision naming 512 shards exhausts the budget on every pass and is never removed (R-P506 (2): eight such revisions never purged across 20 publications; S37/reviewer-p93/REPORT-e20cefda.md:51).
criteria.proof: The P99 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P99.PG1 in src/units/P99/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: No order of deletions can strand a part: the purge deletes the parts a shard names before that shard, or both in one deletion call, so a purge that stops at any call (its budget, PurgeStopped at src/config/publication.ts:1281, or a failed deletion) leaves every part it has not deleted reachable by the next pass through a stored shard or a stored revision; shown with the purge stopped after each deletion call in turn. Today orphansOf queues a shard's key (publication.ts:1402) before the parts behind it (:1404), sweep groups the keys by directory in that order (:1421–1422) and deletes them 1,000 to a call (:1436), so a stop between the shard directory's call and the part directory's leaves parts whose shard is gone, which the next pass no longer reaches (the shard read answers null, :1381–1383) (R-P506 (3), latent under today's budget; S37/reviewer-p93/REPORT-e20cefda.md:52).
criteria.proof: The P99 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P99.PG2 in src/units/P99/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

tickets.title: A browser that drew while the salt version was unknown (**amendment 13, E24, 2026-10-28**)

authority.locator: E24 · section 2 of amendment 13, "Done when" (P95's delivery review, R-P531 (1); in force by section 3 row 1, R-P544)
authority.requirement: the head script adopts the table's number when it holds null, without treating that as a rotation; the SDK bundles regenerated within their budgets; the jsdom leg shows the next rotation repainting once.

tickets.outcome: A browser whose class was drawn while its tenant read an unknown salt version takes the table's number on its next landing without a repaint, so the next salt rotation repaints its default row once, as on any other browser.

criteria.observable: On both hosts, in jsdom with the built head script (public/sdk/edge-head.js, as P84's harness runs it, src/units/P84/LEDGER.unit.test.ts:616), a browser whose stored class was drawn while its tenant read a null salt version (opt_head.arm.saltVersion null) and that holds no engine-known experiment, landing on a page whose context table names a number (holdout.saltVersion): keeps its class and paints as that class paints today, not the default row of a rotation, and stores the table's number in place of the null without treating it as a rotation; at the next salt rotation (the table naming the next number) it paints the default row once and draws its class again, and the landing after paints its class's row. A browser holding a number, a browser holding null on a table that names null, and the known-visitor branch, which reads the experiment the SDK records from each answer (src/sdk/head.ts:152–154; src/sdk/listen.ts:298–301), behave as today (LOCK). Today the head-script-only branch (head.ts:155–158) takes rotated from moved (:146), false whenever either side is null, and rewrites the stored salt version only on a fresh draw (:147–150), so a held null stays null and every later rotation is missed (R-P531 (1); S39/reviewer-p95/REPORT-44f9bbc4.md:65).

tickets.title: A malformed page-view id answered as what it is (**amendment 13, E26, 2026-10-28**)

authority.locator: E26 · section 2 of amendment 13, "Done when" (the 401 diagnosis, R-P541; in force by section 3 row 1, R-P544)
authority.requirement: the decision routes refuse a malformed `pageInstance` with `400 Invalid page instance` before any work, as they do a malformed `arm`; kit 02 states the format.

tickets.outcome: A decision request whose page-view id is malformed is refused at once as the request error it is, 400 Invalid page instance, on every decision path, and a valid id is answered as today.

criteria.observable: On both hosts, a decision request whose pageInstance is outside 1–128 characters of A-Za-z0-9_- (the empty string, a space, a comma, a slash, or 129 characters) answers 400 { ok: false, error: 'Invalid page instance' } before any work: on GET /v1/{tenant}/decisions/snapshot (the query's pageInstance) and on its POST with a session, nothing decided, nothing captured to the ledger or the ring and no render offer minted; at the first-request door (a POST with no session), before a session is issued or a shopper object created, with Cache-Control no-store as the door answers a malformed arm (src/routes/decisions.ts:1132). Today snapshotContext admits any string up to 128 characters on POST (decisions.ts:1021–1024) and any value on GET (:987–1001), the route decides (:1294) with the id as the offer (:1312), and only the render offer's mint refuses it (src/content/renderOffer.ts:62, by isEventNonce, src/events/actionTypes.ts:45–46), answered 401 Shopper session unavailable (src/identity/sessionAuthority.ts:766–767) after the decision's work, for a shopper with tracking consent on a page with a rendered-v1 slot (src/content/service.ts:1230–1234); the door answers a spaced id 200 with no offer, and its catch answers every other snapshotContext failure 401 (decisions.ts:1130–1133) (S42/analyst-401/DIAGNOSIS.md §1).
criteria.proof: The P101 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P101.PI1 in src/units/P101/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.

criteria.observable: LOCK, on both hosts: a valid id behaves as today: the SDK's ids (crypto.randomUUID or its base-36 fallback, src/sdk/host.ts:34–36, set at src/sdk/listen.ts:452 and :534; src/sdk/server.ts:165) and a 128-character id of A-Za-z0-9_- get their render offers and their acknowledgements are admitted; a request with no pageInstance answers 200 with no render offer (src/routes/decisions.ts:1312); the five other request errors keep their answers (decisions.ts:1221–1242) and the door's other refusals stay 401 (decisions.ts:1126–1134).
criteria.proof: The P101 acceptance command runs the tests named unit:P101.PI2 in src/units/P101/LEDGER.unit.test.ts and they pass, and the program integration gate command exits 0 at the same artifact revision.
